speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are here presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to begin my assessment, please describe the onset, severity, and any specific characteristics of the pain. Additionally, have you noticed any fever, chills, nausea, or changes in your urinary frequency?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis)

The patient's history of recurrent UTIs and current presentation of visible hematuria with right flank pain, in the absence of trauma or dialysis, strongly suggests a kidney stone or potentially a chronic infection like chronic pyelonephritis. I will need to review imaging to confirm the presence of a calculus. REQUEST IMAGES: KUB_X-Ray and Non-Contrast CT Abdomen.
